name: RANK.EQ
description: RANK.EQ returns the rank (position) of a number in a list, giving tied values the same rank. It is the modern replacement for the legacy RANK function.
tldr: Ranks a value in a list; ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value whose rank you want to find.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The list (range or array) of numbers to rank against.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional. 0 or omitted = descending (largest = rank 1); any nonzero value = ascending (smallest = rank 1).

basicExample.description: Rank of 20 when it appears twice
basicExample.explanation: The two 20s are the 2nd and 3rd largest, so both receive rank 2.

advancedExamples.title: Ties skip the next rank
advancedExamples.scenario: Ranking the largest value after a tie
advancedExamples.description: Because two values share rank 2, the following distinct value jumps to rank 4.
advancedExamples.explanation: Both 20s are rank 2, so 30 becomes rank 4, skipping rank 3.

advancedExamples.title: Ascending ranking with a tie
advancedExamples.description: With order = 1 the smallest value is rank 1 and ties still share a rank.
advancedExamples.explanation: In ascending order 10=1, then the two 20s share rank 2.

howItWorks: RANK.EQ compares a value to the numbers in the reference. By default (order 0) the largest value gets rank 1; order 1 ranks smallest to largest. Equal values are given the same rank, and the following rank is incremented past the tie (so two values at rank 2 leave the next value at rank 4). It is functionally identical to the legacy RANK and returns #N/A if the value is not found.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the rank.

limitations: Ties share a rank and subsequent ranks are skipped, which can distort rank-based statistics.
Cannot produce averaged ranks for ties; use RANK.AVG for that.
Only ranks against numbers; text in the reference is ignored.

commonErrors.cause: The number is not present in the reference list.
commonErrors.fix: Confirm the value exists in the range you are ranking against.
Pass 1 as the third argument to rank ascending.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports RANK.EQ with identical syntax and behavior to Excel 2010+.

faq.question: Is RANK.EQ the same as RANK?
faq.answer: Yes. RANK.EQ is the name introduced in Excel 2010; RANK is preserved for compatibility and behaves the same.

faq.question: How is it different from RANK.AVG?
faq.answer: RANK.AVG gives tied values their average rank (e.g. 2.5), while RANK.EQ gives both the same whole rank and skips the next.

faq.question: Why does the next rank get skipped?
faq.answer: Because two values occupy the same rank, the sequence continues after the tie, so the next distinct value is ranked one higher than the tie count.
